notes:
Cleaning up is more yours to decide, and DiskAtlas says more about what it found.

- **Your own files can be chosen.** Tick them, or add a folder from the details panel. They
  are still never suggested or ticked for you. The review shows them in a group of their own
  and asks you to confirm before they go to the Trash. Folders macOS keeps, such as
  Documents or Pictures, are never removed whole; what is inside them can be.
- **Right-click anything** in Map, Rings, List or Age to add it to the cleanup with
  everything inside it, show it in Finder, or ignore it in suggestions.
- **After a scan**, a card says how much can be cleared safely, one click from the review.
  Beside it: dependencies of projects you have not touched for 90 days, worktrees with no
  work in progress, and local AI models. In the review each is a switch, off until you turn
  it on.
- **Project dependencies apart from build output.** node_modules and .venv have a quick win
  of their own, since getting them back means a reinstall. Every row names its project and
  how long it has been idle, with one button that ticks the idle ones.
- **Each AI model on its own row.** Hugging Face and LM Studio models can be ticked one by
  one; the whole store folder could not be.
- **Worktrees:** git worktrees made by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or by hand, anywhere on the
  disk, with what git says about each. Only one with nothing unfinished can be ticked, and
  git forgets it after it moves.
- **Folders that could not be read are explained.** Most are closed to every app by macOS,
  which Full Disk Access does not change. The banner now says how many of each kind, lists
  them on request, and only points to Settings when access would help.
- **Updates:** a copy of DiskAtlas that runs outside Applications now says to move it there,
  instead of failing to update. Release notes show their headings and lists properly.
